tldr: EasyNav introduces a modular ROS 2 navigation architecture centered on an explicit shared navigation state, decoupling mapping, localization, planning, and control for heterogeneous robots, and demonstrates significant latency and resource reductions over Nav2 in real-world indoor/outdoor experiments.
tldr_zh: EasyNav 提出了一种以显式共享导航状态为核心的模块化 ROS 2 导航架构，解耦了建图、定位、规划和控制，可在多种异构机器人环境中通用，并在真实室内外实验中相比 Nav2 大幅降低了延迟和资源占用。
summary_zh: 大多数机器人导航栈隐式地将建图、定位、规划与控制绑定到特定的表征形式和数据流上，导致系统架构难以扩展、难以进行实验对比，也难以对端到端时序进行推理。这一问题在异构场景中尤为突出，因为此类场景中多种空间表征、感知模态和坐标系并存，并且以不同速率演化。本文提出一种以显式、共享的导航状态为核心的导航架构，该状态作为各模块组件之间唯一的交互接口。通过约束建图、定位、规划与控制仅基于这一共享状态运行，系统能够在明确的兼容性和时序契约下实现可互换、与表征无关的流水线。我们将该架构实现为EasyNav——一个开源的ROS 2框架，并通过真实机器人实验进行验证，实验内容包括基于激光感知的室内导航，以及基于GPS和3D LiDAR的多层路线大规模室内外导航。在与Nav2在相同条件下的对比中，EasyNav将反应延迟在室内从377毫秒降低至33毫秒，在室外从71毫秒降低至8毫秒，同时CPU和内存占用也更低。

title: Cooperative Transport of Unknown Objects by Distributed Effort Regulation in Multi-agent Systems
summary: A distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy is proposed for objects of unknown shape, size, geometry, mass and mass distribution without any prior knowledge about the object or number of robots involved in the transportation process. Robots follow the boundary of the object and dynamically determine viable pushing points. A novel object-model-free heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation method is proposed to promote goal-directed object motion; robots regulate their pushing effort using individual and collective heading errors. Robots dynamically relocate around the object boundary if a pushing point is lost or the required pushing effort exceeds its capability to correct its heading. The proposed method is validated using simple and complex shapes with convex and non-convex boundary regions and dynamically changing weight distribution of objects. Detailed analysis on the effects of robot distribution and initial object pose on the transportation performance in terms of required time and path efficiency is also presented. Scalability analysis revealed that object transportation time is dependent on the number of pushing surfaces available which in turn depends on the object size, shape, and set inter-robot safety distance. The proposed system yielded highly efficient object paths with consistent elapsed transport times over several trials robust to external disturbances such as non-uniform friction between contacting surfaces and robot wheel slip.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy for unknown objects using heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation, validated in simulations with various shapes and disturbances.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种面向未知物体的分布式多机器人搬运策略，基于航向误差驱动的推力调节，并在多种形状和扰动下进行了仿真验证。
summary_zh: 针对形状、尺寸、几何结构、质量及质量分布未知，且无任何先验信息或参与搬运机器人数量信息的多机器人物体运输问题，提出了一种分布式多机器人协同搬运策略。机器人在物体边界移动，动态确定可行的推动点。本文提出了一种新颖的、基于航向误差的无物体模型推力调节方法，以促进物体向目标运动；各机器人通过个体航向误差与群体航向误差调节自身推力。若推动点失效，或所需推力超出其调整航向的能力，机器人将沿物体边界动态重新布置位置。通过简单及复杂形状、凸与凹边界区域以及动态变化的物体重量分布，验证了该方法的有效性。详细分析了机器人分布和物体初始姿态对搬运性能的影响，包括所需时间和路径效率。可扩展性分析揭示，物体搬运时间取决于可用推动表面的数量，而后者又取决于物体尺寸、形状及设定的机器人间安全距离。所述系统生成了高效的物体搬运路径，多次试验中的搬运时间具有一致性，对非均匀接触面摩擦及机器人车轮打滑等外部扰动表现出良好鲁棒性。

title: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
summary: A frozen diffusion generator may need to change several output properties while preserving others. We study when guidance faithfully realizes such a structured request and whether local inverse correction improves its direction. Our account links this benefit to the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian: conditioning alone is insufficient. Spectral steering combines a request-specific cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction and fixed-time relinearization for finite edits. Scalar nulls and matched-movement controls test the predicted mechanism. Across 8,923 instances in a retrospectively identified local regime, predicted and realized gains correlate at Spearman 0.79, versus -0.11 for condition number. Experiments span images, audio, robotics, and control and planning, including complex character motion generation. On 50 paired inpainting cases, four corrections improve unobserved-pixel PSNR over Adam by 3.25 dB at equal total derivative traversals. Together, the analysis and controls connect request-dependent geometry to directional gains and establish where these gains translate into downstream performance.
tldr: This paper analyzes guidance in frozen diffusion generators, introducing spectral steering with local inverse geometry to improve directional control while preserving other properties, validated across images, audio, robotics, and control/planning tasks including character motion generation.
tldr_zh: 该论文分析了冻结扩散生成器中的引导机制，提出了结合局部逆几何的频谱转向方法，以在保持其他属性的同时改善方向控制，并在图像、音频、机器人以及控制和规划任务（包括角色运动生成）中进行了验证。
summary_zh: 一个冻结的扩散生成器可能需要改变多个输出属性，同时保持其他属性不变。我们研究了引导在何种情况下能够忠实地实现这种结构化请求，以及局部逆校正是否能改善其方向。我们的解释将该收益与请求和目标特定剩余采样器雅可比矩阵之间的交互联系起来：仅靠条件约束是不够的。谱引导结合了请求特定的余弦增益预测器、阻尼逆校正以及用于有限编辑的固定时间重线性化。标量零点和匹配运动控制用于检验所提出的机制。在回顾性识别的局部区域中的8，923个实例中，预测增益与实际增益的斯皮尔曼相关系数为0.79，而条件数的相关系数为-0.11。实验涵盖图像、音频、机器人技术以及控制与规划，包括复杂角色运动生成。在50个配对的修复案例中，四种校正方法在相同的总导数遍历次数下，将未观测像素的PSNR较Adam提高了3.25 dB。综合来看，分析与控制将请求相关的几何特性与方向性增益联系起来，并确定了这些增益在何种情况下转化为下游性能的提升。

title: Latent World Modeling for Point-Cloud Video Pretraining
summary: Masked modeling is the dominant self-supervised paradigm for point-cloud videos. However, it leaks the information it is meant to predict, whether it reconstructs masked points as in MAE-style methods or predicts their latent features. Because point-cloud tokens are anchored at points sampled from each frame, querying a target at its own position reveals where its geometry has moved, in reconstruction and latent prediction alike. For latent predictors, random spatio-temporal masks introduce a further shortcut, as visible frames on both sides of each target allow interpolation rather than forecasting. The pretext task thus reduces to completion. Once the target positions are withheld, a masked latent predictor performs only slightly better than copying the last frame. To remove this leakage, we propose PointWM, a latent world model that turns completion into forecasting by predicting the features and geometry of future frames from strictly earlier context. Each target is queried only with its last-seen position and timestamp, while a latent action learned without annotations is meant to capture the part of the future that the past leaves undetermined. On HOI4D action segmentation with a P4Transformer backbone, PointWM improves F1@50 over training from scratch by 24.9 offline and 29.1 under strictly causal inference. These results show the promise of latent world models as a leakage-free pretraining paradigm for point-cloud videos.Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/InitalZ/PointWM.
tldr: PointWM introduces a latent world model pretraining paradigm for point-cloud videos that avoids information leakage by predicting future frames' features and geometry from strictly earlier context, achieving significant improvements in action segmentation on HOI4D.
tldr_zh: PointWM提出了一种用于点云视频预训练的无泄漏潜在世界模型范式，通过仅从早期上下文预测未来帧的特征和几何形状，在HOI4D动作分割上取得了显著改进。
summary_zh: 掩码建模是点云视频自监督学习的主导范式。然而，该方法会泄露其本应预测的信息——无论是像MAE风格方法那样重建被掩蔽的点，还是预测其潜在特征。由于点云令牌锚定于每帧中采样的点位置，在重建和潜在特征预测中，若在其自身位置查询目标，便会暴露该点几何位置的移动轨迹。对于潜在特征预测器，随机时空掩码引入了进一步的捷径：每个目标两侧的可见帧允许插值而非外推，从而使预文本任务退化为补全任务。一旦隐藏目标位置，掩码潜在预测器的表现仅略优于直接复制最后一帧。为消除该信息泄露，我们提出PointWM，一种潜在世界模型，通过仅基于更早的上下文预测未来帧的特征与几何，将补全转变为预测。每个目标仅以其最后出现的位置和时间戳进行查询，而无需标注学习到的潜在动作则旨在捕捉过去无法确定的未来部分。在基于P4Transformer骨干网络的HOI4D动作分割任务中，PointWM相较于从头训练在离线场景下F1@50提升24.9，在严格因果推断下提升29.1。这些结果表明，潜在世界模型有望成为点云视频无泄露预训练范式的有效方案。我们的代码已公开于https://github.com/InitalZ/PointWM。

title: Conditional Optimal Transport and Triangular Maps for Imitation Learning
summary: We introduce a unified formulation of imitation learning from demonstrations as a conditional sampling problem solved by triangular transport: a policy is the second block of a triangular map that transports a reference distribution to the conditional distribution of the action chunk given the observation history. Unlike in Diffusion Policy, where it is a fixed Gaussian, the reference becomes a design variable; we take it to be the empirical distribution of the demonstrated action chunks and introduce three instances of the formulation: an optimal transport policy (OTP), a flow matching policy (FMP), and a stochastic interpolant policy (SIP). On the Push-T and robomimic Square tasks, the three policies are competitive in task performance with Diffusion Policy and Consistency Policy while using considerably smaller networks and shorter training, and the informative reference accounts for a substantial part of their performance when few network evaluations are used. The three instances offer different trade-offs rather than a single best method: OTP generates an action chunk with a single evaluation of the smallest network (0.23 million parameters on Push-T) and is suitable for settings in which inference time and model size matter, whereas SIP attains the highest scores among the proposed policies at a higher cost.
tldr: This paper unifies imitation learning as conditional sampling via triangular transport, proposing three policies (OTP, FMP, SIP) that achieve competitive performance with fewer parameters and shorter training than Diffusion Policy on Push-T and Square tasks.
tldr_zh: 本文将对模仿学习统一为通过三角传输实现的条件采样，提出三种策略（OTP、FMP、SIP），在Push-T和Square任务中以更少的参数和更短的训练时间达到与Diffusion Policy相当的性能。
summary_zh: 我们提出了一种统一的模仿学习形式化方法，将演示中的模仿学习视为一个条件采样问题，并通过三角输运求解：策略是三角映射的第二块，该映射将参考分布输运到给定观测历史条件下动作块的条件分布。与扩散策略中参考分布为固定高斯分布不同，这里的参考分布成为设计变量；我们将其取为演示动作块的经验分布，并引入该形式化方法的三个实例：最优输运策略（OTP）、流匹配策略（FMP）和随机插值策略（SIP）。在Push-T和robomimic Square任务上，这三种策略在任务性能上与扩散策略和一致性策略相当，同时使用更小的网络和更短的训练时间；在少量网络评估的情况下，信息丰富的参考分布对其性能贡献显著。这三个实例提供了不同的权衡，而非单一的最优方法：OTP通过最小网络（在Push-T上为23万参数）的单次评估生成动作块，适用于推理时间和模型规模重要的场景；而SIP在较高成本下获得了所提策略中的最高得分。

title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
summary: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.
tldr: This paper proposes a score-based diffusion framework for stochastic closure modeling in reduced-order simulations, using indirect offline learning and online data assimilation without direct closure data. It demonstrates improved predictions and generalization on turbulent flow simulations, with relevance to world models for AI agents.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种基于评分扩散模型的随机闭包建模框架，通过间接离线学习和在线数据同化，在无需直接闭包数据的情况下改进湍流模拟的预测和泛化能力，并提及对AI智能体世界模型的潜在应用。
summary_zh: 随机闭合建模是大规模复杂（例如多尺度、多物理场）系统降阶建模中的一个新兴领域，在此类系统中，数值模拟中计算上可承受的降阶物理描述（例如增材制造的数字孪生、AI智能体的世界模型）不可避免地会导致信息损失，而经典确定性闭合方法无法有效解决这一问题。然而，学习随机闭合通常需要闭合数据，这些数据难以从测量中获取，或者使用第一性原理模拟计算的成本往往高得令人望而却步。在本工作中，我们开发了一种基于分数扩散模型的随机闭合建模框架，利用间接离线训练和在线数据同化，而无需直接获取闭合数据。二维湍流数值实验表明，间接离线学习能够捕获关键的闭合统计特征并改善系统状态的预测。此外，将学习到的闭合模型与已知物理动力学相结合，相比直接预测系统状态的纯数据驱动模型，在不同流态下具有更好的泛化能力。与基于高斯假设的标准数据同化方法相比，后验分数同化能更好地表征所学闭合模型的非高斯特征，其与状态级数据同化的结合进一步改善了系统状态的预测。该框架能够在力学和工程问题中复杂动力系统的现实且具有挑战性的场景下实现随机闭合建模，在这些场景中，模型形式不确定性的非高斯统计特征不可忽略（例如，由于系统动力学和/或观测的非线性），且真实的闭合数据在离线学习和在线同化中均不可获得。

title: A Geometric Observer for Visual-Inertial Odometry using Optical-Flow Constraints
summary: This paper presents a geometric observer for monocular visual-inertial odometry driven by individual optical-flow constraints. For each tracked point, the bearing and its rotationally compensated derivative give a depth-free homogeneous constraint on the body-frame velocity. These constraints enter the innovation of an observer on the gravity-augmented group $\mathbb{SE}_3(3)$ through a Riccati gain, without estimating depths or reconstructing the direction of motion. The auxiliary gravity state makes the six-dimensional body-frame velocity-gravity error dynamics independent of the attitude correction, and their uniform observability is shown to be equivalent to persistent excitation of a matrix formed from the inertial bearings and their derivatives. Under this condition, the body-frame velocity and gravity errors converge globally and uniformly exponentially, and a gravity-based attitude correction renders the combined velocity, gravity, and reduced-attitude error almost globally asymptotically stable and locally uniformly exponentially stable. Simulations illustrate the excitation condition, recovery from initial errors, and sensitivity to perturbed measurements.
tldr: This paper proposes a geometric observer on SE_3(3) for monocular visual-inertial odometry that uses optical-flow constraints to estimate body-frame velocity and gravity without depth estimation, with proven convergence under persistent excitation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种基于SE_3(3)群的几何观察器，利用光流约束进行单目视觉惯性里程计，无需深度估计即可估计机体速度和重力，并证明在持续激励条件下收敛。

title: DynLimit: A Simulation Benchmark for Dynamics-Critical Planning and Control
summary: Experiments near vehicle handling limits must keep three questions apart: what a maneuver requests, what the closed-loop system executes, and whether the task is completed. We present DynLimit, a simulation platform that organizes this process end to end. Scenarios are composed from road, friction, obstacle, and reference objects; planners and controllers attach through a shared observation and control interface; a vehicle adapter runs either a license-free four-wheel model or an external dynamics solver; and synchronized records feed task evaluation, replay, and response inspection. The platform carries a task-oriented evaluation method that pairs a prescribed reference demand with a sampled passing set and event-aligned diagnosis. Across eight task families, three friction environments, and three reference-assisted baseline chains we executed 450 runs: 360 nominal, 18 locally refined, and 72 with prescribed initial offsets. Method differences depend on the task family, equal aggregate pass counts arise from different passing cells, and local refinement narrows two sampled transitions without locating a continuous boundary. Two case comparisons show why sideslip or tire-utilization peaks cannot replace task constraints. The three views therefore stay distinct in every reported run: an outcome can be traced from the prescribed demand, through the executed response, to the task rule that decided it. Code is available at https://github.com/Yang2581/dynlimit
tldr: DynLimit is a simulation benchmark for evaluating dynamics-critical planning and control near vehicle handling limits, with a task-oriented evaluation method that distinguishes maneuver demand, closed-loop execution, and task completion. It includes eight task families, three friction environments, and 450 runs, providing a platform for reproducible assessment of trajectory planners and controllers.
tldr_zh: DynLimit是一个用于评估车辆动力学极限附近规划与控制的仿真基准平台，区分了操作请求、闭环执行和任务完成三个过程，包含八个任务族、三个摩擦环境和450次运行，为轨迹规划器和控制器提供可复现的评估平台。

title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
summary: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. Experiments with 6 representative SLAM systems show that existing methods fail to maintain both localization accuracy and trajectory continuity across the full set of water--land transitions, exhibiting transition-induced drift, trajectory discontinuities, and tracking failures. M-CROSS is publicly available https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MCross-Dataset
tldr: M-CROSS is the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water-land transitions, providing synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements with medium-dependent degradation models and a transition-aware evaluation protocol. Experiments with six representative SLAM systems show existing methods fail to maintain accuracy and continuity across transitions.
tldr_zh: M-CROSS 是首个用于水陆连续过渡场景下 SLAM 的多传感器仿真数据集和基准，提供同步的 LiDAR、声纳、立体相机、IMU、DVL 和深度测量，并带有介质相关的降级模型和过渡感知评估协议。对六种代表性 SLAM 系统的实验表明，现有方法在过渡过程中无法保持准确性和连续性。

title: PSK: A Matrix-Free Single-Loop Method for K-Level Physics-Based Control
summary: Physics-based control is central to robot learning, but differentiating through implicit physics steps typically requires Hessian or Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) linear solves; we ask whether gradient steps suffice. Each simulation step minimizes an energy under many contact and collision constraints. Without constraints, we view control over $K$ steps as $K$-level optimization with strongly convex lower levels, recast as one min--max problem. Our Penalized Single-loop $K$-level method (PSK) uses only gradients and a projection, updates all levels in parallel, and reaches an $ε$-stationary control in $O(ε^{-3})$ iterations, with a $K$-independent exponent but a $K$-dependent constant. Contact-rich constraints, however, typically violate a constraint qualification (CQ). We replace each constraint by a smooth wall that acts on a band of constant width. Under mild assumptions that need no CQ, every exact solution of the banded lower levels is then feasible and banded Fritz--John, and PSK keeps the $O(ε^{-3})$ complexity. Without a CQ that is uniform in the band width, however, a shrinking band loses the $K$-independent exponent: with width $ε$ and fixed $K\geq2$, deterministic zero-respecting methods need $Ω(ε^{-(K+3)/4})$ calls on a hard instance whose control dimension grows with $1/ε$. We prove our assumptions for smoothed kinematic and dynamic multi-robot navigation among segment obstacles. In navigation experiments, PSK, tuned per case, reaches every goal with sixteen levels and, at equal time, reaches a lower loss than tuned unrolling in 17 of 18 cases, while implicit differentiation is lower in 10.
tldr: This paper proposes a matrix-free single-loop optimization method for physics-based control over K simulation steps, achieving O(ε^-3) complexity and demonstrating lower loss than unrolling in navigation experiments.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种无矩阵单循环优化方法，用于K步物理仿真控制，达到O(ε^-3)复杂度，并在导航实验中比展开方法获得更低的损失。

title: Aerial Person Detection under Edge Constraints: Held-Out Evaluation and Edge-Ground Verification
summary: A search drone sees a missing person as a few pixels, carries a small computer, and shares a narrow radio link. We study person detection under those limits; the primary evaluations were declared before they ran, and later analyses are marked exploratory. In an exploratory comparison, holding out recording blocks inferred from thermal frame identifiers cut recall at a fixed false-alarm target from 32.7% to 12.3%. With nothing tuned on test blocks, a 46,000-parameter detector gated by a contrast cue finds 10.4% of people against 5.7% for the same network applied everywhere. A standard detector, YOLO11n, trained under the same folds finds 54.5% at a similar false-alarm rate for about eleven times the arithmetic, and on our 4K field footage at 117 m has a walking person among its top 16 detections in up to 92% of frames against 74% for our board. Run alone, YOLO11n's thresholds set at one location overshot their false-alarm target 1.7 to 3.4 times at new locations, and its best configuration at altitude cost 4 to 24 standard passes per frame. Re-scoring its 16 best crops (154 KB per frame) with an 842,000-parameter ground model, thresholds frozen on a validation location, raised recall from 44.9% to 53.7% against the same 16 crops with YOLO's own scores; in a post hoc paired analysis over 15 test locations the gain was +8.8 points [+2.4, +12.5]. Pooled false detections fell from 0.86 to 0.64 per frame, but that paired change was not distinguishable from zero. Coverage of a still person in earth tones was very low for both detectors in the clips we flew.
tldr: This paper evaluates person detection from drones under edge constraints, comparing a lightweight detector against YOLO11n and showing that gating and re-scoring with a ground model can improve recall at low false-alarm rates.
tldr_zh: 本文评估了边缘约束下无人机对行人的检测，对比轻量检测器与YOLO11n，并表明通过对比线索门控和地面模型重打分可在低误报率下提高召回率。

title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
summary: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive density-driven control framework for coordinating multiple UAVs to track and map dynamic air pollution plumes, using predictive propagation and sensor-driven surrogate updates.
tldr_zh: 本文提出一种自适应密度驱动控制框架，用于协调多架无人机跟踪和绘制动态空气污染羽流，利用预测性传播和传感器驱动的替代更新。

title: "Don't Leave the Task Unfinished": Persistence-Driven Violations under Quiet Oversight
summary: LLM agents are increasingly given long, multi-step tasks to carry out, with the user reviewing little of what happens in between. Persistence, the tendency to keep working until a task is complete, is installed on purpose to improve performance on long tasks. Long-horizon tasks are typically complex, and the user's instruction can fall short of what the work actually requires, or conflict with the constraints the agent encounters in the task. We study what persistence does on long-horizon operations tasks that cannot be solved without breaking a documented constraint. We find that the agent pursues completion to the point of violating the constraint, and that a critically engaged user lowers the violation rate. Persistence takes violations from 29.2% to 58.3% across four models. Violations stay high wherever oversight goes quiet, whether the user is silent, assenting, or delegating with expressed trust. Only a questioning user, who asks for the basis of each action before allowing the next, brings the rate back to roughly the level measured without persistence. Practitioners should treat high persistence as a setting that carries a safety cost, and should recognize that the cost appears when oversight goes quiet. Safety here is better cast as a property of the human-AI pair than of the model alone. Project page: https://francis21c.github.io/quiet-oversight/

title: A Geometric Understanding of Denoising Autoencoder with Applications to Image Denoising
summary: Denoising autoencoders have shown strong empirical performance in recovering clean data from their noisy observations, yet their underlying statistical behavior remains underexplored. In this paper, we study denoising autoencoders under the manifold hypothesis, assuming that clean data are supported on low-dimensional smooth manifolds embedded in a high-dimensional ambient space, while noisy observations are generated by isotropic Gaussian noise. We establish generalization guarantees in three geometric scenarios: a single manifold, a pairwise separated finite union of manifolds, and a finite union of intersecting manifolds. Using local chart representations, partitions of unity, and neural network approximation, we derive upper bounds for the expected squared reconstruction error for denoising autoencoder. In the single-manifold and separated-union scenarios, the error consists of a sample-dependent statistical term of order $n^{-2/(d+2)}\log^4 n$, a residual term of order $dσ^2/D$ caused by tangential noise, and an exponentially small tail term associated with failure of the manifold projection. Here $D$ is the data ambient dimension, $d$ is the intrinsic dimension of the clean-data manifold, and $σ^2$ is the expected squared noise magnitude. In the scenario of intersecting manifolds, we further identify an additional ambiguity term determined by the probability mass near the intersection neighborhood. Numerical experiments on synthetic manifolds and real image datasets support the predicted sample-size scaling law and illustrate the additional reconstruction ambiguity near manifold intersections.

title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
summary: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

title: A Threshold-Free Visual-Semantic Matching Metric for Evaluating Consistency in Subject-Driven Image Generation
summary: In subject-driven text-to-image generation, quantitatively evaluating localized visual consistency across varying poses and environments remains a major challenge. Existing metrics either rely on global image embeddings (CLIP, DINO) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that pool spatial representations and miss fine-grained textural artifacts, or depend on scalar threshold-gated dense metrics such as Visual-Semantic Matching (VSM) that suffer from point-alignment dropouts, severe threshold sensitivity, and score instability. To overcome these limitations, we propose TF-VSM, a fully continuous, threshold-free visual-consistency metric paired with an extended feature-disentanglement retraining schedule for dual-branch ResNet feature-aggregation networks. Rather than enforcing rigid binary cutoffs $(T_s,T_v)$, TF-VSM weights every object point by a non-linear semantic match confidence $w_j=ReLU(\hat{s}_j)^2$ and continuously integrates visual similarity over all consistency levels $r\in[0,1]$, yielding a closed-form confidence-weighted score without any hand-tuned hyperparameters. On a controlled 100-pair benchmark with ground-truth inpainting oracles, TF-VSM attains Pearson $0.638$ and Spearman $0.674$ oracle correlation, improving over the pretrained VSM baseline ($0.454/0.589$) by $+0.171/+0.116$ after retraining, and drastically outperforming CLIP ($-0.052/-0.004$), DINO ($0.087/0.121$), and VLMs ($0.096/0.003$). Six diagnostic ablations confirm that smooth confidence weighting is the right mechanism, that hard semantic gating is brittle (dropping to $0.533$ Pearson at $T_s{=}0.8$), and that the threshold-free metric is essentially invariant to the training-time loss balance $α$ that the thresholded metric still depends on.

title: A phase diagram for training and inference in language models
summary: A language model is a complex system whose behavior is determined jointly by the Transformer and the corpus, yet how the representation geometry in the Transformer relates to the actual behavior of language models remains open. We analyze how the representation geometry changes along the forward propagation of actual language models and characterize the representation geometry of a document at a given layer by two collective coordinates, document distinguishability and document dimension. On the phase diagram spanned by these collective coordinates, inference is represented as a flow along depth. We find that, for untrained models, depending on their initialization scale, most of the 156 inference flows move toward the collapse and noise regions of the phase diagram. By contrast, the inference flows of 8 trained models from 5 architecture families all enter and reside in the central region of the phase diagram. Describing the evolution of the flows with a discrete Langevin equation, we find that the difference between the inference flows of untrained runs and those of trained models reduces to whether the effective force on the flows in this region is of saddle or stable-node type. On Pythia-1.4B, we interpret the training process as a phase transition. These results give a unified gateway to the relation between representation geometry and language-model behavior.

title: A plug-in energy-balance freezing module for transformer frost nowcasting without leaf-sensor inputs
summary: Frost protection requires local warnings where leaf-sensor inputs are unavailable. In the frost literature we surveyed, physics entered machine-learning models through inputs, numerical-model coupling, or losses, rather than model structure. We develop a transformer-compatible module that embeds leaf energy-balance physics in freezing-probability forecasts: an energy-balance temperature reference and a learned residual predict leaf temperature, which drives a multiplicative gate imposing a temperature-dependent probability cap. We mathematically prove conditional monotonicity and an alarm boundary, and test whether placing the same information in the output pathway or in attention yields different benefits. We evaluated 12 hourly leads at 19 Korean stations over five frost seasons, with and without leaf-sensor inputs. In the 2025-2026 hold-out season without these inputs, our time-token transformer (PET-E) achieved a lead-mean critical success index (CSI) of 0.516 versus 0.478 for fixed-configuration, joint-lead LightGBM, with significant gains at all 12 leads, and the fraction of alarms at observed leaf temperatures of at least 2 degrees C fell from 0.087 to 0.051 relative to the unmodified backbone. Across the hold-out and a retrospective 2024-2025 evaluation, the module reduced Brier scores and warm-surface alarm fractions in both the time-token transformer and iTransformer, with no significant CSI decrease at any lead. At held-out stations without static or leaf-sensor inputs, both module-equipped backbones exceeded LightGBM at all 12 leads (CSI 0.468 and 0.467 versus 0.437). In the time-token backbone, the temperature pathway reduced this alarm fraction in all four settings, whereas the attention prior increased CSI in three. These findings link an explicit temperature-dependent probability cap to improved forecasts and distinguish output-side from attention-based embedding.

title: AGPF: Dynamic Source Selection for Feature Pyramid Fusion
summary:
Feature pyramids provide dense predictors with features at several spatial resolutions. However, it remains largely unexplored which pyramid levels each output location should aggregate information from. We investigate this question by allowing each output location to attend to features from every pyramid level and measuring how attention is distributed across scales. Surprisingly, locations on the finest output grid allocate approximately 75\% of their attention to features two levels coarser, rather than to the current or adjacent levels. Even on the same output grid, the balance shifts toward coarser features as object size increases.
  These observations motivate Asymmetric Global Pyramid Fusion (AGPF), a neck that preserves the original output grids while allowing each location to dynamically select its contextual sources across scales. Each location interacts with a multiscale memory whose features are aligned in image coordinates, enabling flexible cross-scale aggregation without altering prediction resolutions. Compared with FPN, AGPF improves all 19 object detection and all seven instance segmentation configurations evaluated on COCO. A single fusion block improves Cascade Mask R-CNN by 1.7 box AP and 2.3 mask AP, and the gains consistently transfer to semantic and panoptic segmentation.

title: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
summary: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. Passkeys solved the analogous problem for humans, but they require a human gesture on every use and cannot be operated by an autonomous process. We present the Agent Authenticator, a design that gives agents passkey-grade authentication properties: per-service hardware-bound keys, no shared secrets, origin binding enforced by the runtime rather than the model, normalized attestation of the execution environment, human-signed scoped mandates, and cross-device human approval for high-risk actions. The same protocol serves agents on developer laptops and in cloud enclaves, and it deploys as a profile over existing mechanisms, MCP authorization, OAuth token exchange including the Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant, git and SSH, rather than as a new identity system. The authenticator also produces a signed, hash-chained record of each action it authorizes. We analyze the design against a threat model centered on prompt injection and same-host compromise, map it onto five documented incidents, and discuss its limits.

title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
summary: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

title: Ambiguous Examples Help, But Full Data Wins: Revisiting Dataset Cartography for Extractive Adversarial QA
summary: Dataset cartography argues that training dynamics can reveal regions of a dataset that matter differently for learning: easy-to-learn examples aid optimization, hard-to-learn examples often expose annotation problems, and ambiguous examples contribute strongly to out-of-distribution generalization. A striking implication of the original work is that a model trained on only 33% ambiguous examples can outperform full-data training on several OOD evaluations, including a QNLI reformulation of SQuAD evaluated on Adversarial SQuAD. We revisit this claim in a stricter setting: open-ended extractive question answering, where models must predict answer spans rather than classify question-sentence pairs. For each encoder family, we compute clean-source SQuAD training dynamics, train on full, random, easy-ranked, ambiguous-ranked, and hard-ranked subsets, and evaluate robustness on adversarial-only AddSent and AddOneSent rows. Ambiguous-ranked 33% subsets beat random 33% subsets on exact-match accuracy in all 14 model-evaluation cells and on F1 in 12/14 cells. However, full-data training beats ambiguous-ranked training in 12/14 exact-match cells and 12/14 F1 cells, with mean full-minus-ambiguous gains of 3.40 EM and 4.10 F1. The most thoroughly replicated ELECTRA-small panel is also the main exception to the ambiguous-over-random F1 gains. These results show that clean-source cartography remains useful for reduced-data selection, but its OOD advantage does not carry over as a general replacement for full-data training in extractive adversarial QA.

title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
summary: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. Experiments show consistent geometric separation of consonant categories, with Silhouette Coefficients exceeding 0.5 and origin-based ROC-AUC scores above 0.86. Furthermore, evaluations using real dysarthric speech achieved a high ROC-AUC of 0.897 in screening for unclear pronunciations. Perturbation tests confirm orthogonal temporal and spectral shifts, yielding a physically interpretable mapping for rehabilitation.

title: Architecting the Corporate AI Infrastructure: The Evolving Roles of AI Governance Committees and Chief Ethics Officers
summary: The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into core business operations has created an urgent need for robust corporate governance infrastructures capable of managing complex ethical, legal, and operational risks. While organizations have increasingly adopted high-level AI ethics principles, a critical implementation gap persists: fewer than half of organizations that cite AI governance as a boardroom priority have a formalized governance framework in place. This paper addresses that gap by proposing a structured corporate AI governance architecture (CAIGA) centred on two mutually reinforcing pillars. First, it examines the evolving mandate of specialized C-suite roles, specifically Chief Privacy Officers (CPOs) and Chief Ethics Officers (ChEOs), in formalizing accountability for AI usage across the enterprise. Second, it argues that cross-functional AI Governance Committees, uniting representatives from legal, technology, data science, cybersecurity, and business units, are the essential organizational mechanism for translating ethical principles into operational decisions, including strategic go/no-go approvals for new AI initiatives. Drawing on a conceptual review of peer-reviewed governance literature, regulatory frameworks including the EU AI Act, and documented industry practice, this paper contributes a replicable governance architecture that embeds clear accountability policies, structured risk management workflows, and an organization-wide ethical AI culture. The framework is illustrated through application to the financial services sector. The findings have direct implications for corporate leaders, risk professionals, and policymakers navigating the rapidly evolving global AI regulatory landscape.

title: Asking the right question is key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) scientists pursue discovery through a chain of hypotheses, fitting candidate models to existing observations and often choosing experiments where those models disagree most. Yet when early data miss a narrow feature, model selection favors simple curves that agree across the unmea- sured gap, so disagreement-guided search has no reason to look where the new phenomenon lies. When we tested two frontier AI scientists, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1-Sol, across 32 closed-loop trials with a narrow peak omitted from the starting data, both sampled inside the peak region less often than random search. Surprisingly, the agent that followed model disagreement more closely missed the peak in all 32 trials, whereas discovery succeeded when experiments probed the unmeasured gap early and followed up across the anomaly. Asking the right question, rather than testing only where current models disagree, is therefore key to AI discovery in a chain of hypotheses.

title: Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
summary: Reinforcement learning can make automated red-teaming more successful while narrowing the attacks it produces. Co-training an attacker and a defender with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been reported to reduce attacker diversity. This experiment reproduces attack diversity reduction using three runs with a Qwen2.5-14B attacker and a Phi-4-mini defender trained by direct preference optimization (DPO). The attacker receives a success-only reward and uses a length-unbiased loss, bounded updates, warm-up and ratio clipping. The attacker is evaluated on 26 AdvBench behaviors. Training ended after 12 rounds, following a decision based on development checkpoints, so the reported intervals are nominal. Attack Diversity Retention (ADR) compares the within-behavior of the trained attacker spread with the untrained attacker. In order for an attack diversity to be consider as having been reduced, a criterion requires the ADR to be below a 0.75 target with a 95% confidence interval together with continued attacker effectiveness. Therefore, if an attacker narrows its attack vector by 25% consistently its considered less diverse. After 24 attacker and 12 defender LORA-based updates, ADR for the three runs were 0.63, 0.61 and 0.63, respectively. Each run met the criterion at round 12; the earlier checks at rounds 4 and 8 fell short. Despite attacks being less diverse, attack success continued to improve as the attacker was updated after each training run.

title: Autonomous Multi-modal Agents for ITOps Observability
summary: ITOps observability products must integrate data from different tools and systems. We present ITOps Observability Studio, a multi-modal multi-agent system that orchestrates observability workflows through collaborative AI agents. Its three-tier architecture features inter-agent communication, specialized LLM-powered agents for data access, schema operations and visualization, and unified tool integration. The system supports natural language to GraphQL translation, GraphQL schema generation, schema mapping, trace data lifecycle management and multi-tool workflows for reliability engineering. Its agents are instrumented with agent analytics, so that their model and tool calls can be traced. We evaluate each agent on its own benchmark, scored against gold answers where they exist and by a model judge for schema mapping and chart quality. Query generation on a public benchmark and routing work well with a current open model, and the data lifecycle management agent solves most of its scenarios. The evaluation exposed defects that only appear when prompts, parsers and serving stacks are tested together, and we report them together with their fixes.

title: BadGCL: Towards Persistent Backdoor Attack on Graph Continual Learning Systems
summary: Backdoor attacks pose a persistent security threat to machine learning systems, yet their behavior under graph continual learning (GCL) remains underexplored. Conventional graph backdoor attacks often lose effectiveness as models are updated across successive tasks, creating the impression that continual updates naturally weaken malicious associations. This work reveals a contrasting vulnerability: knowledge-preservation mechanisms in GCL can also preserve early injected backdoors when the poisoned update is compatible with the clean-task signal being retained. For graph data, this risk is amplified by structural triggers, which are embedded into the message-passing paths of graph neural networks (GNNs) and can induce stable representation shifts across tasks. To expose this risk, we propose BadGCL, a model-agnostic framework for persistent backdoor attacks under a strict early-stage intervention setting. BadGCL learns topology-aware structural triggers using a gradient mutual-information objective that couples poisoned gradients with clean-task optimization signals, together with a propagation consistency objective that stabilizes trigger-induced effects through graph message passing. We provide theoretical analysis showing that gradient compatibility and propagation stability jointly support long-term backdoor persistence under benign continual updates. Extensive experiments across task-IL and class-IL protocols, four GCL benchmarks, and diverse victim systems show that BadGCL achieves persistent attack effectiveness with limited clean-utility degradation, substantially outperforming graph and continual-learning backdoor baselines and remaining robust against representative defenses.

title: Barron Approximation and locally optimal weight densities for shallow neural networks
summary:
Mean field theories provide optimization results for shallow neural networks by analyzing the weight distribution in infinite width limits. Corresponding results for finite sized networks are obtained by particle approximations, for which sharp quantitative bounds are still an open problem.
  In this paper, we consider a modified mean field loss, which allows a more fine grained control over finite sized networks. We prove convexity and equidistribution properties, which directly lead to Barron type approximation results for networks sampled from local loss minimizers. We demonstrate that particle approximations of the new loss function naturally lead to gradient descent methods with dropout type regularization.

title: Before the Word: Name Information in Description-Derived States of Small Language Models, With and Without Naming Failure
summary: The tip-of-the-tongue (TOT) state, knowing an object but not its name, motivates this study as an analogy only. We ask whether small language models form a name-predictive state from a name-free description, and whether it differs when naming fails but description selection succeeds. In an internally pre-registered study (a frozen document, no external registry) of Qwen2-0.5B, SmolLM2-1.7B and Phi-3-mini with 200 items, we combine a similarity read-out, a Patchscopes-style read-out and activation patching with matched controls. H1 (name information in the state) was supported in all nine model-by-description-type combinations; the agreement rule was met by the similarity measure together with patching, while Patchscopes stayed near chance. Post-hoc robustness checks after internal review (logit lens, single-position patch, manipulation check) temper this reading: name information in middle layers is clearest under the multi-position patch and the similarity measure, and weak under single-position patching at 50% depth. H2' (description-paraphrase consistency of name-free states not lower in failure items) is mixed: the SmolLM2 deficit test is significant under the pre-registered specification but not robust; Phi-3 non-inferiority holds across margins and a word-overlap covariate, although its bootstrap interval includes zero; Qwen2-0.5B is inconclusive. A capacity explanation remains untested. We report vehicle-level signals only, not meaning.

title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
summary: AI agents are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, yet existing evaluations provide limited assurance that they behave consistently with their intended characteristics across diverse interactions. We introduce an evaluation framework for measuring the behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents. The framework operationalizes agent behavior along five measurable axes and uses a standardized evaluation battery spanning six socially salient interaction settings to assess behavioral differentiation, consistency, and drift. Controlled persona configurations serve as experimental anchors, enabling systematic testing of whether intended behavioral differences persist across contexts rather than appearing only as stylistic variation. Preliminary analyses demonstrate measurable differentiation across configurations and suggest associations between behavioral profiles and interaction outcomes. By shifting the focus from persona design to behavioral assurance, this work provides a foundation for evaluating whether socially deployed AI agents behave as intended, consistently and measurably, across the situations in which users encounter them.

title: Bellman Residual Bracketing: Resolving the Sample Complexity of Discounted and Average-Reward RL
summary: We study the sample complexity of the empirical planning or plug-in approach for reinforcement learning (RL) with a generative model. We show the discounted plug-in approach finds an $\varepsilon$-optimal policy with $O(SA (1-γ)^{-3} \varepsilon^{-2} \log(SA/δ))$ samples, where $S, A, γ, δ$ are the state and action sizes, discount factor, and failure probability, respectively. In the average-reward setting, we show that discounted plug-in and direct (undiscounted) plug-in achieve $O(SAH\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ and $O(SAD\varepsilon^{-2}\log(SA/δ))$ complexities, respectively, where $H$ upper-bounds the optimal bias span and $D$ is the diameter. Combining with our lower bounds for nonadaptive generative models, these results resolve the minimax sample complexity of discounted RL and average-reward RL --- in both the span- and diameter-based classes --- up to constant factors. Our main technical contribution is a novel Bellman residual bracketing technique which improves the efficiency of prior absorbing-MDP-based concentration analyses.

title: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
summary: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. Across three studies on two model families (240, 112 and 108 runs), enforcement during execution produced no oracle-detected violation in 104 paired runs, against 21 to 55% of runs without rules, and no loss of functional correctness in the two confirmatory studies. In the confirmatory study on tasks aimed at known failure situations (Study 3, protocol hashed before the first run), enforcement lowered the share of violating runs by 31 percentage points relative to no rules (Holm-adjusted p = 0.014); the 17-point difference from prompted rules was not significant (p = 0.12), and neither was any contrast in Study 2, where only 3 of 14 tasks produced a violation. Prompted rules removed some violation types but not recursive deletes of scratch directories, and checks after generation repaired file edits but not commands that had already run. That enforcement satisfies the rules it enforces is expected by construction; what the data add is where prompting falls short, the absence of a functional cost, and the limits of the rules and of the oracle themselves. The studies use low-cost models and one small fixture.

title: Beyond the Training Cameras: Coverage-Controlled Probes of Viewing Direction in Frozen Vision Models
summary: Vision models are trained on 2D images of a 3D world. Do their hidden features encode the direction from which the camera views a scene, and if so, in what form? We study the relative viewing direction $α$ of two objects in rendered scenes where both object centres stay at fixed pixels while the camera moves, so that perspective, shading and shadows change but the projected layout does not. In eight pretrained models, from diffusion models to self-supervised and image-text encoders, $α$ is encoded in a strikingly simple form: a single two-dimensional plane in the hidden space, shared across scenes, in which the difference between the two objects' features traces $(\cosα, \sinα)$. The plane keeps its orientation when lighting, colours, floors and object shapes change. This encoding is more than a summary of a few visible measurements: readouts fitted on one set of camera paths stay accurate at camera positions outside their range in seven of the eight models, whereas decoders of the measured object and shadow geometry, equally accurate within that range, fail there. In the diffusion transformer PixArt-$α$, the plane forms abruptly at a single block and carries direction information to later blocks, yet editing it changes the objects rather than the generated viewpoint. We also examine how this encoding carries over to scanned real objects.

title: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation
summary: As globalization accelerates the demand for seamless cross-border enterprise collaboration, multilingual translation remains bottlenecked by insufficient domain-specific terminology, rigid terminology translation, weak instruction-following capabilities, and high inference latency in long-instruction scenarios. To overcome these barriers, we propose Bridging the Terminology Gap (BTG), a data-centric framework. First, BTG mines cross-lingual term alignments from domain documents and leverages LLMs to synthesize terminology-rich parallel corpora. Second, a hybrid filtering strategy combining heuristics and XCOMET scoring ensures high data fidelity. Third, a two-stage training paradigm employs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for targeted terminology injection, followed by reinforcement learning (RL) to refine output preferences, effectively balancing domain knowledge integration with model reliability. Extensive offline evaluations (e.g., XCOMET, GEMBA, Acc@T) and online human assessments demonstrate significant improvements in terminology accuracy and instruction-following capabilities, validating the effectiveness of our framework, which is now deployed on our cross-border collaboration platform.

title: CECAR: Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing Accelerates On-Device Inference of MoE LLMs
summary: Despite growing interest in on-device LLM deployment, large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models remain impractical on resource-constrained devices, as sparse expert activation still requires all expert weights to be memory-resident. To address this, we identify three key observations for on-device MoE inference: (a) cache hit rates are fundamentally bounded even under Belady's optimal policy; (b) these bounds are insufficient for low-latency on-device inference; and (c) prior cache-aware routing based on binary cache presence can induce routing instability. Based on these insights, we propose CECAR (Cache & Expert Co-Aware Routing), a MoE inference system that jointly considers expert routing and cache management. Unlike prior cache-aware routing methods, CECAR uses an ML-based cache policy to predict the expected reuse distance of each expert and prioritizes routing and execution toward experts with smaller predicted reuse distances. On the Qwen3-30B-A3B model, CECAR achieves 12.5 tokens/s on a consumer-grade GPU with only 16 GB of VRAM, where non-resident experts are fetched from SSD, delivering a 4.5x speedup over conventional MoE inference and exceeding the decode speed of baselines that keep the entire model fully resident in DRAM. Code is available at https://github.com/hoonki2002/CECAR.

title: Can AI Judge You? An Empirical Audit of Deployment Readiness in LLM-assisted Hiring Systems
summary: Delegating resume screening to large language models (LLMs) requires organizations to establish whether they can distinguish candidates by relevant qualifications while allowing only authorized users to change screening rules or approve exceptions. To this end, we develop a system architecture that separates candidate evidence, evaluation, permission controls, and assessment record, and empirically examine two complementary dimensions of its deployment readiness. First, we assess its operational readiness on four LLMs using a controlled experiment on 210 resumes across 14 job roles and six decision interfaces. Second, we assess its compliance readiness by testing how it handles unauthorized user requests and instructions embedded in resumes. We find that operational performance depends on the choice of evaluation interface: scalar scores generally distinguish qualification changes better than simple pass/fail judgments, while comparative judgments are sensitive to presentation order. Explicit permission rules and separation of resume content from instructions reduce unauthorized compliance, to a varying degree of effectiveness across LLMs and usage contexts. Finally, we find that LLM evaluators often diverge between their decisions and offered justifications. Going beyond simply evaluating LLMs for hiring tasks, our framework supports an audit of a fully configured resume evaluation system to enable its deployment decision.

title: Can decision models extract clinical data from cancer pathology reports? An evaluation of accuracy, calibration, and failure modes
summary: Decision models are a new class of language model that, instead of generating text, choose one option per question from a fixed list and return a probability for every option. They have not yet been evaluated on clinical text. We evaluated two open-weights decision models, Nimble 9B and Tev1 4B, for extracting 25 fields from 1,113 oral cavity cancer pathology reports from a single centre, against a prospectively maintained clinical database. We compared them with two generative models: Qwen3.5 9B, run locally, and GLM-5.3-flash, run through a cloud API. Tev1 reached a mean field accuracy of 0.917 (95% CI 0.913 to 0.920), the same as Qwen3.5 9B (0.918; p = 0.26), and was four times faster (15 s against 61 s per report). Nimble reached 0.862 and GLM-5.3-flash 0.986. Both decision models matched GLM-5.3-flash on simple dichotomous categories. They were weak on measurements binned into categories, on fields whose correct answer was not reported, and on some complex decisions (e.g. involved margins). We found that the main cause of the inferior performance of Nimble's came from asking 25 questions in one request: with two questions per request, its accuracy improved. Pooled over fields, the returned probabilities were well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.022 and 0.026), but they did not flag systematic errors within single fields. A simulated strategy of sending answers with a probability below 0.94 to GLM-5.3-flash raised Tev1's accuracy to 0.982, with 38% of answers escalated. Decision models can extract explicitly stated findings from pathology reports quickly on local hardware and return useful probabilities. They should be validated in the configuration in which they will be used, restricted to the fields in which they are reliable, and combined with other methods for numeric values.

title: CapCover Filter: Semantic Approximate Membership Queries over Embeddings
summary:
Determining whether an embedding is sufficiently similar to any vector in a vector store without performing a nearest-neighbor search can substantially improve query throughput in vector-store systems. We study Semantic Approximate Membership Queries (SAMQs), which allow queries to be rejected when no indexed vector meets the requested similarity threshold, while guaranteeing no false negatives.
  We introduce CapCover Filter, a geometric data structure that summarizes a set of embeddings using spherical caps. Its representation is independent of the query threshold, allowing a single filter to support arbitrary thresholds without reconstruction. We evaluate alternative construction and quantization methods, compare CapCover Filter with competing filters, and measure its impact on query throughput.
  Across five real-world datasets, at a cosine similarity threshold of 0.95, CapCover Filter eliminates approximately 20--100\% of index accesses while using only 2\% of the raw (FP32) embedding memory. When placed before a FAISS flat index, it improves query throughput by up to 382\% and by approximately 116\% on average across the five datasets, while returning the same range-search result. We also evaluate lower similarity thresholds. Our results show that CapCover Filter can substantially improve vector-store throughput when similarity thresholds are tight, retrieval is expensive, and indexed embeddings are highly clustered. We release an optimized implementation of CapCover Filter and its evaluation framework.

title: Clinician Assessment of Laryngeal Disease with Auditory AI before Laryngoscopy: A Paired Reader Study
summary:
Background: Before laryngoscopy, clinicians assess the likely cause of hoarseness and whether to suspect a precancerous or malignant lesion. Whether voice-based artificial intelligence (AI) supports pre-laryngoscopic categorization is unknown.
  Methods: We developed an auditory large language model that generates a patient-level assessment card (provisional category, voice-quality ratings, and rationale) and a prespecified malignancy alert from voice recordings, patient information, and acoustic measures obtained before laryngoscopy at one center. We evaluated both in a held-out test set and a later cohort. In a sequential reader study, 32 otolaryngology clinicians categorized held-out cases without AI and, 1 to 2 weeks later, reviewed their initial categories with the card (without the alert).
  Results: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31). Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect. Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation. The malignancy alert flagged 85.7% and 86.8% of precancerous or malignant lesions. Sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions increased from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.3 to 42.0).
  Conclusions: In this single-center study, clinicians' pre-laryngoscopic categorization accuracy was higher after reviewing the AI assessment card, although the sequential design cannot fully separate AI assistance from reassessment; gains depended on model correctness without clearly selective adoption. Randomized and external evaluations, including of the malignancy alert, are needed.

title: CoSyDelay: Cognitive Symbolic Regression for Traffic Delay Estimation
summary: Trustworthy estimation of traffic delays at signalized intersections is critical for modern transportation systems, as it supports proactive traffic control for congestion mitigation. Existing analytical methods often rely on idealized assumptions that limit their accuracy under complex traffic conditions, whereas data-driven methods may achieve strong estimation performance but usually lack transparent structures, which reduces confidence in their practical application. To address these limitations, we propose CoSyDelay, a cognitive symbolic regression (SR) framework for automatically deriving explicit and physically consistent empirical delay estimation expressions (DEEs). Specifically, CoSyDelay decomposes intersection-level delay estimation into turning-movement-level subproblems, thereby reducing the complexity of the symbolic search. During DEE learning, CoSyDelay constructs domain-informed symbolic inputs from traffic variables. Large language models (LLMs) are employed as symbolic search operators to iteratively generate and refine candidate expression structures, whose movement-specific coefficients are subsequently calibrated using approach-level delay labels. A composite fitness function evaluates the learned DEEs jointly in terms of estimation accuracy and compliance with specified traffic-delay principles. Experimental results on multiple signalized intersections demonstrate that the resulting expressions achieve competitive estimation performance while maintaining physical consistency, thereby supporting trustworthy delay estimation. Source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/ForrestXie9/CoSyDelay.

title: Communication-Efficient Distributionally Robust Federated Averaging with Multi-Source Data
summary: Federated learning trains a shared model from distributed client data. The deployment risk is typically specified through two approximations: each unknown local distribution is replaced by its empirical distribution, and the unknown deployment mixture across clients is replaced by empirical or prescribed training weights. Existing robust methods usually address one approximation at a time through local distributional ambiguity sets or worst-case client mixtures. However, joint treatment of both approximations remains underexplored. To address this gap, we construct a global ambiguity set formed by admissible mixtures of client-wise Wasserstein ambiguity sets, yielding a distributionally robust optimization formulation. The construction allows client-dependent ambiguity radii, preserves client-wise separability of the objective function, and yields a high-probability out-of-sample guarantee for the resulting robust problem. We then introduce a penalty-based approximation of this formulation and develop a communication-efficient algorithm called BiDRO-FedAvg, for which we establish a convergence guarantee. We validate the proposed framework through a market-demand prediction simulation.

title: Conditional Asset Pricing Transformer
summary: In this paper, we propose a conditional asset pricing transformer (CAP-T) that captures nonlinear interactions among firms through attention to forecast excess returns. In the first stage, a transformer estimates conditional expected returns, and kernel-weighted principal component analysis of its residuals estimates the local factor loading space. Projecting the conditional mean onto this space separates factor risk compensation from conditional mispricing. Then, in the second stage, separate transformers learn these two components, whose predictions are combined to forecast returns. As a result, the proposed framework decomposes returns into conditional mispricing, factor risk compensation, a centered factor component, and an unpredictable innovation. We establish approximation and generalization bounds and characterize how first-stage prediction errors propagate through local factor estimation and component learning, providing statistical guaranties for conditional mispricing, factor loadings, and factor risk premia. Finally, simulations and empirical studies demonstrate the predictive and interpretive benefits of the proposed method.

title: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
summary: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. Experiments on our MLM dataset show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both comprehensive quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.

title: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
summary:
Coding agents can synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, allowing the resulting program to act with zero inference model calls. But for long horizon tasks, two challenges arise: local improvements can hurt final success and switching to a new objective requires another expensive synthesis run. We propose a framework that first develops competence by refining the policy through a feedback cascade, moving from episode returns to hierarchical goals and belief updates which can be scored densely from simulator. In the Craftax game, a partially observed and procedurally generated environment, refinements via episode level feedback stall at <1% final-level arrival, whereas with the feedback cascade the optimized policy reaches the final stage 50% of time (28% final boss defeats). Furthermore, to make this competence reusable towards new goals, we factor the previous controller into an environment interpreter $I$ (models, memory, skills) and a rule program $p_0$, and we show that coding agents can optimize a reusable goal compiler $C_θ$ that maps structured tasks $g$ into new rule programs $p_g$. Across five independent compiler searches trained only on short tasks, the resulting compilers successfully transfer zero-shot to longer tasks without any task-specific tuning nor inference-time LLM calls: continuation-scored feedback and a fixed machine with an editable program together turn a single-task competent policy into a reusable one.
  Code at: https://github.com/vicgalle/craftax-program-policies

title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
summary: Video creative plagiarism refers to the unauthorized reproduction of creative ideas across videos despite substantial differences in visual appearance, posing a new challenge to video copyright protection. However, existing video copy detection methods primarily focus on visual content similarity, struggling to capture abstract creative that are entangled with specific visual realizations. To address this issue, we introduce a novel task, named Video Creative Plagiarism Detection (VCPD), and propose an iterative creative evidence tracing framework, termed CreaTrace, to verify creative similarity and accurately localize the corresponding evidence segments. Specifically, we design a Multimodal Semantic Event Segmentation strategy to divide similar long videos into coherent narrative events, facilitating event-level dataset construction and retrieving similar segments. Based on these events, CreaTrace employs Coarse Creative Matching to identify candidate event pairs through narrative semantics and camera language. Then CreaTrace presents Creative Decoupling to disentangle abstract creative patterns from specific visual realizations. Meanwhile, Creative Swap Contrastive Learning is devised to enhance creative consistency through cross-realization feature swapping. Benefiting from the above designs, our CreaTrace enables accurate creative similarity detection and temporal localization, while providing interpretable evidence report. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of CreaTrace across diverse creative plagiarism scenarios.

title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
summary: Pretraining data curation decides what a model learns from, yet what makes a document worth learning from depends on what the model already knows. Influence-driven selectors already rank documents to improve one run; we argue that training-data attribution should steer pretraining by identifying testable data properties that become reusable curation criteria, evaluated on new data against cheaper selectors at matched total cost, discovery included. A document ranking is consumed by the run it was computed for, whereas an explained data property can be tested across corpora and checkpoints, especially where familiar quality signals diverge from measured usefulness. Because historical contribution, an understandable explanation, and future data value require distinct evidence, we specify a feedback loop that interprets attributed sources, tests candidate data changes, and states for five claim types what evidence each requires and what none establishes. We close with a falsifiable comparison against perplexity, classifier, and mixing baselines at equal total compute.

title: Data-Driven Heuristic-Guided Business Process Redesign
summary: Business process redesign (BPR) has a long-standing catalog of best-practice redesign heuristics, yet, applying them remains a mostly manual task that requires extensive domain knowledge. Despite recent advances using Large Language Models (LLMs) for conversational process model redesign, limitations remain. For example, redesign is user-driven instead of data-driven and is not guided by best practices such as the redesign heuristics. Moreover, only one change can be handled at a time. To address these limitations, given an event log and a BPMN model, we present the DH-BPR framework to realize data-driven heuristic-guided BPR using LLMs. To design DH-BPR, we first conducted an analysis of which redesign heuristics can be automatically detected and applied given information contained in an event log such as the fraction of cases that bypass an activity. Based on this, DH-BPR detects and validates heuristic candidates through a combination of rule-based techniques and an LLM. After that, DH-BPR jointly designs and records an application plan for valid candidates, before finally yielding a redesigned BPMN model and an updated resource model (the way resources execute the process).
